dedupe_keys.name: hrsa health professional shortage areas and medically underserved areas populations data united states

description: These data list the federally designated Health Professional Shortage Areas (HPSAs) and Medically Underserved Areas and Populations (MUA/Ps) in the United States, published by the Health Resources and Services Administration on its data warehouse. HPSA designations cover primary care, dental health and mental health and are geographic, population or facility designations with a score, status, rural status and update date; MUA/P records carry type, status and rural flags. Coverage is every state and territory of the United States. The site offers search by state and county, an address lookup for up to 100 addresses, map galleries, and eligibility analysers for the Medicare physician bonus and telehealth payments. Designation files are free to download in XLSX and CSV from the data downloads page, as US government information with a usage disclaimer, and are updated continuously with quarterly summaries and Federal Register notices. Caveats: designations follow federal criteria and lag local change, and some counties are designated only for population groups. Simulation uses: weighting health access vulnerability in hazard exposure and equity analyses, choosing sites for temporary care after disasters, and flagging areas where facility loss would be hardest to absorb. Related records: the HRSA workforce projections (data-hrsa-health-workforce-projections) and the Area Deprivation Index (data-neighborhood-atlas-area-deprivation-index) are complementary.
